newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia PM defends expenses row handling.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia PM defends expenses row handling.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Thursday defended his handling of the controversy surrounding the resignation of a government senator, saying he had kept parliament properly informed of the sequence of events.

The Australian Opposition accused Howard on Thursday of misleading the public about the exact time that he became aware of a police investigation into allegations that senator Bob Woods had fiddled his expenses.
"The guidelines require that you correct any inadvertent misleading, that you do it as soon as practicable. I believe that I have done that," Howard told parliament.
"I believe I have complied with the guidelines in full. I believe I have been honest and open in my dealings."
On Tuesday, a television interviewer asked Howard when Woods had first advised him of the investigation into the allegedly dishonest expense claims.
Howard said Woods had told him 10 days before.
But the government Senate leader Robert Hill told the upper house on Wednesday that Attorney-General Daryl Williams had advised Howard of the investigation late last year.
Howard told parliament on Thursday he had forgotten about the earlier meeting with Williams until he was reminded about it late on Wednesday afternoon.
